lines.text: It was an ordinary Monday morning. People were rushing to work, children were walking to school, and traffic filled the streets.
Until every phone in the city received the same emergency alert.

alert.body:
A nuclear missile has been detected heading toward the United States.
Impact location currently unknown.
Seek immediate shelter. Await further instructions.

lines.text: Nobody moved.
Then the television screens inside Times Square switched to an emergency broadcast.
A reporter was visibly struggling to speak.
Officials are asking everyone to remain calm. We don't know who launched it. We don't know why.
Suddenly, the broadcast went black.
Inside an apartment on the thirty-second floor, nineteen-year-old Alex received a phone call from his father, who worked at a government facility.
Alex, listen carefully. You need to get your little sister and
A second later, Alex received a text.

lines.bubble: Whatever happens, DO NOT trust the emergency broadcast.

lines.text: Then another message arrived.

lines.bubble: Your father is lying. He knows who launched it.

lines.text: Alex looked at his sister. She was crying.
A second emergency alert appeared. But this one was different.

alert.body: “Citizens of the United States. This is not an attack. This is a warning. You have been living alongside something you were never supposed to discover.”

lines.text: The screen went black.

alert.body: “Citizens of the United States. This is not an attack. This is a warning. You have been living alongside something you were never supposed to discover.”

lines.text: Alex's father finally called again.
Son, there's something I never told you. Your mother didn't die in that accident.
The lights went out.
The entire city fell silent.
Alex looked outside. A bright light appeared on the horizon.
And his phone displayed one final message.

choice.title: WHAT DOES ALEX DO?
options: A. Take his sister to the underground shelter.
B. Call his father and demand the truth.
D. Escape the city with his sister.
